channel.title: World News
channel.description: Aggregated headlines linking to original publishers

item.title: Netanyahu closes West Bank after thwarted potential ‘major attack’
item.description: Five people were injured in a shooting at an Israeli military checkpoint in the West Bank, sparking Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu to close off the entire area.

item.title: France awaits Moody's verdict: Downgrade widely expected as debt fears grow
item.description: France's cost of living protests come as the country struggles with its increasing public debt. Concerns over these public finances have pushed the nation's 10-year government bond yield above 5% for the first time since 2002—making borrowing costs higher. Oliver Davis, Professor and Head of the French Department at University College Cork, is our guest.

item.title: War in the Middle East: Israel launches West Bank operations
item.description: Palestinian militants wounded five Israelis in an attack on Friday before being killed in a shootout with soldiers, leading Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu to order a lockdown in the occupied West Bank days before Israeli elections. Details by Kethevane Gorjestani, FRANCE 24's International Affairs Editor.

item.title: At least seven dead after shooting at church in Jordan - reports
item.description: At least seven people have been killed after gunmen opened fire during a funeral a church in Jordan, reports say.

item.title: Brazil's tense presidential run-off campaign feels like a psychological thriller
item.description: Insults traded on social media and a combative debate have intensified the pressure ahead of a fiercely contested presidential run-off on Sunday, with only a few points separating leftist pro-union President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva and far-right challenger Flavio Bolsonaro, the son of former president and Trump ally Jair Bolsonaro.

item.title: Authorities investigating whether first Kenya and Nigeria Ebola cases crossed paths
item.description: Nigeria this week recorded its first case of Ebola in the current outbreak, which has spread from the epicenter in Congo to several other African countries.

item.title: Singapore's longevity industry: The quest for eternal youth
item.description: In Singapore, the quest for eternal youth is no longer just a billionaire's fantasy. It's becoming big business. High-tech clinics, longevity labs and specialist companies all promise the same thing: slowing down the ageing process. From continuous metabolic monitoring and genetic testing to supplements and oxygen therapy, every aspect of the body is measured and optimised.

item.title: Kremlin says first tanker of Russian diesel sets sail for the US
item.description: The Kremlin says that a first tanker carrying Russian diesel to the United States has set sail under a new import agreement

item.title: REPLAY: Laurent Nunez holds presser on security arrangements ahead of protests
item.description: French Interior Minister Laurent Nunez held a press conference on security arrangements ahead of upcoming protests. He announced that 70,000 security forces would be mobilised on October 24 to keep order.

item.title: WATCH: Woman makes history swimming the entire California coast
item.description: ABC News' Danny New talks to Catherine Breed, who made history by swimming the nearly 900-mile route in just 111 days.

item.title: French authorities ban some student protests after weekend looting and clashes
item.description: Dozens of protesters took to the Paris streets on Thursday despite bans on demonstrations ordered in multiple French cities following a weekend of clashes and widespread looting that marked France’s most violent unrest in years.

item.title: SA faces rising tension as foreign national is killed amid anti-migrant protests
item.description: South African police are investigating the murder of a foreign national after violent protests by anti-immigrant groups swept through the central business district in Durban. The latest death follows months of violent rallies in which at least 10 foreigners were killed and several other countries on the continent raced to repatriate their people. Details by FRANCE 24's correspondent Eunice Masson.

item.title: One killed, four including child injured in drive-by shooting in Paris suburb
item.description: One person was killed Friday and four were injured, including a 12-year-old child, when a man opened fire from a vehicle in the town of Trappes west of Paris, police said. French prosecutors said that they were investigating the shooting as a suspected terrorist attack. At least two of the victims have immigrant backgrounds.

item.title: WATCH: New Jersey mayor defends charging critic during town hall meeting
item.description: Chaos unfolded during a town hall meeting in Pemberton, New Jersey, after Mayor Matthew Bianchini charged at a critic before being restrained by a former police chief.

item.title: Claude Monet: 'Iris' becomes most expensive artwork sold at auction in France
item.description: "Iris," a monumental painting by Impressionist Claude Monet, sold for 50 million euros ($56 million) in Paris on Thursday, becoming the most expensive artwork ever sold at auction in France.

item.title: French authorities call for videos of looting to identify rioters
item.description: To identify rioters across France last weekend, French authorities are calling on people who filmed scenes of looting to assist the investigation by handing the videos in. That is an unprecedented decision - one causing debate.

item.title: Art: Claude Monet's 'Iris' fetches 50M euros at Paris auction
item.description: "Iris," a monumental painting by Impressionist Claude Monet, sold for 50 million euros ($56 million) including buyer fees in Paris on Thursday, has become the most expensive artwork ever sold at auction in France.

item.title: UN searches for new Secretary-General as Antonio Guterres term comes to an end
item.description: Antonio Guterres's term as UN Secretary-General is coming to an end. The international organisation is looking for his replacement. Leading candidates are struggling to secure the support they need. Details from FRANCE 24's correspondent in New York, Jessica Le Masurier.

item.title: Netanyahu orders West Bank closure as attack wounds Israelis before election
item.description: Details by FRANCE 24's correspondent in Jerusalem Noga Tarnopolsky.

item.title: Volvo Cars in share price crash as 2,500 job cuts follow sales slump
item.description: Volvo Cars has revealed a further 2,500 job cuts amid a slump in sales that has seen its share price crash to record lows.

item.title: French mayors analyze the political crisis as new protests are expected
item.description: French mayors Emmanuel Gregoire of Paris and Benoit Payan of Marseille have analysed the current political crisis in France and the government's choice to impose curfews in several cities to prevent violence in upcoming protests. This comes in the wake of weekend unrest and riots.

item.title: Across Africa: Ivorian vinyl head's heritage hunt
item.description: This week in Across Africa: Ivorian music lover Cédric Kouamé is on a mission to restore 20th-century African vinyl and bring old-school sounds back to modern playlists. Also, 10 years after Cameroon's worst railway disaster, families are still fighting for justice for the 79 people killed. Finally, in São Tomé and Príncipe, we discover how the islands' rich volcanic soils produce some of the world's most distinctive vanilla.

item.title: Trump defends Ramaswamy ad as top Republicans call for taking it down
item.description: Both Ohio Gov. Mike DeWine and Iowa Republican Senate candidate Rep. Ashley Hinson said his campaign should cease airing the ad.

item.title: DOJ probing Trump ally Corey Lewandowski's actions at DHS after IG referral: Sources
item.description: Lewandowski, a longtime Trump ally, served as ousted DHS Secretary Kristi Noem's top aide

item.title: Trump slams LeBron James over apparent national anthem stretches
item.description: President Donald Trump criticized James for appearing to stretch during the national anthem ahead of his 76ers debut.

item.title: Olympic fever grips Senegal as Dakar hosts Youth Olympic Games
item.description: As Senegal prepares to host the Youth Olympic Games (YOG), the first Olympic event ever organised in Africa, the country is pulling out all the stops to be ready on time. FRANCE 24’s Sarah Sakho and Simon Martin report.

item.title: Marseille's European slump continues with defeat to Sturm Graz
item.description: Marseille conceded their third defeat in three Europa League games on Thursday in Graz, as an early goal was enough to seal the three points for the hosts.

item.title: Buttigieg endorses independent over Democratic nominee in Montana Senate race
item.description: Pete Buttigieg is endorsing independent Montana U.S. Senate candidate Seth Bodnar.

item.title: European football giants to meet in London for NBA basketball talks
item.description: A cluster of European football giants will convene in London next week for talks as they try to finalise a string of deals for European basketball teams worth billions of dollars.

item.title: Items recovered in search for missing fishing boat and crew
item.description: Items belonging to a fishing boat that vanished off the Western Isles have been recovered as searches continue for the vessel and two missing crew members.

item.title: Politics in 'materialist terms': Gen Z in Albania, Italy, France and India protesting for 'fairness'
item.description: Jean-Emile Jammine is pleased to welcome Gökçe Tuncel, Sociologist and post-doctoral researcher associated with the Université Paris-Est Créteil (UPEC). For Tuncel, the wave of youth-led protests across France, Albania, India and Italy reveals more than a succession of localized grievances. It signals the emergence of a political consciousness shaped by material insecurity, institutional disillusionment and an increasingly explicit demand for solidarity and social justice. "What is really striking about this Gen Z movement is how clearly young people see their material conditions," Tuncel observes.

item.title: With jet fuel prices near a record, holiday airfares soar higher
item.description: If you're planning to fly this holiday season, be prepared to pay more than you did last year. The price of jet fuel — one of airlines' biggest expenses — is close to an all-time high in the U.S.

item.title: Major protests in France: French shop owners brace for more unrest
item.description: French President Emmanuel Macron said on Thursday that "illegitimate" protests would be banned in the coming days and blamed "seditious" ultra-left groups and vandals for last weekend's riots and looting.

item.title: NYT reports plans for fresh strikes on Iran after the US midterm elections
item.description: Reza Sayah, our correspondent in Tehran Iran, has more.

item.title: Ivory Coast: Children face serious health risks from lead in paint
item.description: Report by Jean Barrère & Guillaume Gougeon.

item.title: Netanyahu orders army to prepare for full West Bank closure after attack
item.description: The office of Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu ordered the army to prepare for a full closure of the occupied West Bank Friday after Israeli soldiers shot and killed two men who the military said had launched a "terror attack" near the city of Hebron. Emergency services said five people were injured and evacuated to hospitals.

item.title: Africa faces 'complex' Ebola outbreak after spread to Nigeria: WHO
item.description: The World Health Organization warned Thursday that Africa faced a "complex" Ebola outbreak after the virus crossed from east Africa to Nigeria, marking the first case in the west of the continent.

item.title: Israel orders army to prepare to fully close West Bank after two soldiers killed in shooting
item.description: The Israeli government has ordered its army to prepare for a full closure of the occupied West Bank following a shooting near Hebron which killed two soldiers.

item.title: Police officer raped by David Carrick waives anonymity and says Met chief must resign
item.description: A police detective raped by fellow officer and notorious sexual predator David Carrick has called for the head of the Metropolitan Police to resign.

item.title: Man 'sexually obsessed' with stepdaughter jailed for her murder
item.description: A man who had a secret sexual obsession with his stepdaughter before going on to murder her has been jailed for at least 35 years.

item.title: WATCH: 12-year-old 'Captain William' goes viral after Delta DREAM Flight
item.description: Aspiring pilot William Hobson, 12, is winning hearts online after showing off his impressive in-flight lingo aboard Delta’s DREAM Flight.

item.title: Veterans ask federal judge to block Trump's arch unless Congress approves it
item.description: The Justice Department said Wednesday construction will begin on Nov. 5.

item.description: As the Tampa Bay Rays and their fans prepare for the World Series, David Muir reports on how the community rebuilt the city and repair Tropicana Field after Hurricane Milton.

item.description: ABC News' Danny New talks to Jordan Sunshine, a boy in California who found therapy for his anxiety by performing on the streets of Los Angeles.

item.description: The first human case of the Shamonda virus has been detected in France in a person who later died, according to authorities.

item.description: North Korea says it plans to resume propaganda broadcasts targeting South Korea within days along the heavily-armed border between the two countries.

item.description: A Garda investigation has been launched after two bodies were discovered in Ireland.

item.description: A drone strike on a fuel depot in a disputed region on the Sudan-South Sudan border has killed at least 153 people.

item.description: Nigeria has recorded its first case of Ebola during the current outbreak, the country's health ministry has said - as the virus continues to spread internationally.
